package_info.package_versions: N/A (multiple variants targeting South Korean users)
package_info.why_malicious: The FakeCalls Android Trojan impersonates over 20 South Korean financial apps, simulates voice calls with fake bank employees using pre-recorded audio, and exfiltrates private data including audio recordings, contacts, and call logs to attacker-controlled servers. Its primary purpose is to deceive users into divulging sensitive information and to steal private data, constituting clear malicious intent.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user launches the fake banking app or receives a simulated call event
execution_context.file_location: Main activity and supporting classes within the malicious APK (e.g., com.fakecalls.MainActivity, assets/ directory for audio files)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user opens the app or initiates a call, the code displays a fake banking interface, plays pre-recorded audio to simulate a bank employee, records the user's responses via the microphone, collects private data (contacts, call logs, device info), and exfiltrates all gathered information to a remote command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code impersonates legitimate financial applications, simulates phone calls with fake bank employees using pre-recorded audio, records user audio without informed consent, and exfiltrates sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure. These behaviors are designed to deceive users and steal confidential information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate banking app should never simulate calls with fake employees, record user audio without explicit consent, or transmit private data (audio, contacts, call logs) to unknown external servers. Such actions violate user privacy and standard security practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may request microphone access for customer support or voice authentication, but only with clear user consent and without exfiltrating recordings or sensitive data to untrusted servers. Legitimate banking apps do not simulate employee calls using pre-recorded audio.
key_indicators: Impersonation of multiple South Korean financial institutions within the app UI and package name
Simulation of voice calls using pre-recorded audio files stored in the APK assets
Unauthorized audio recording triggered during simulated calls
Collection of contacts, call logs, and device information without user awareness
Exfiltration of recorded audio and private data to remote command-and-control servers

attack_chain.action: User installs the FakeCalls APK, believing it to be a legitimate banking app.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is launched and begins malicious activity.

attack_chain.action: App presents a fake banking interface and prompts the user to initiate a call or responds to an incoming call event.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is engaged in a simulated conversation with a fake bank employee.

attack_chain.action: App plays pre-recorded audio to simulate a bank employee, records the user's responses via the microphone, and collects private data from the device including contacts and call logs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive information and private data are gathered.

attack_chain.action: App exfiltrates the recorded audio and collected data to a remote command-and-control server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen information for further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Android app mimicking multiple South Korean financial institutions in UI and package name
Simulation of voice calls with pre-recorded audio files during app use
Unauthorized audio recording triggered during simulated calls
Collection and exfiltration of contacts, call logs, and audio recordings to external servers
file_indicators: APK package names closely resembling legitimate South Korean banking apps with minor deviations (e.g., typos, extra characters)
Presence of pre-recorded audio files (e.g., .mp3, .wav) within the APK assets directory
Manifest requesting excessive permissions: RECORD_AUDIO, READ_CONTACTS, READ_CALL_LOG, INTERNET, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, READ_PHONE_STATE
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known FakeCalls C2 infrastructure (domains/IPs as identified in threat intelligence feeds)
Unusual data uploads (audio files, contact lists, call logs) during or immediately after simulated calls
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request excessive permissions (microphone, contacts, call logs, network) and whose package names closely resemble but do not exactly match legitimate South Korean banking apps. Analyze app behavior for simulated calls using pre-recorded audio files and check for unauthorized audio recording and exfiltration of sensitive data. Use network monitoring to flag connections to known FakeCalls C2 domains or IPs, and detect suspicious data uploads (especially audio files and contact/call log data) during app use.
